key_insight: Region-aware Mixture of Experts models learn flow-correction forcing that approaches data-assimilation accuracy in an axial compressor without requiring experimental inputs during deployment.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a route to more accurate turbomachinery CFD by incorporating learned corrections into the discretized Navier–Stokes equations.
method: Fuse experimental PIV data with steady fixed-grid RANS and unsteady moving-grid hybrid RANS/LES using a Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Kalman Filter.
Train neural networks on the enriched database to map local velocity, velocity gradients and turbulent viscosity to volume forcing terms.
Use a Mixture of Experts to select and combine learned corrections across different flow regions.
evidence_signal: Against experimental data, the Mixture of Experts shows systematically lower discrepancies than baseline RANS and accuracy very similar to the Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Kalman Filter.
watch_item: Standalone neural models can produce localized errors exceeding baseline RANS near blade tips; robustness beyond the assessed compressor flow is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Assisted Turbulence Modeling via Data Assimilation and Machine Learning for Turbomachinery Flows
